Check a schema

Source: R/data-mapping.R
validate_schema.Rd

Checks a schema's structure and, if it is mapped, its inputs and outputs. Every function that builds or changes a schema – build_schema(), add_step(), update_io(), update_data(), read_tines(), as_schema(), expand_tines() – runs these checks and reports the problems its change introduced; gen_code() and draw_tines() run them before using a schema. Call validate_schema() yourself after editing a schema directly, e.g. with schema$inputs[[2]] <- ....

Structure (an error): the id, objective, decision and rationale fields exist, and ids are present and unique.

Completeness (a message): if some steps have inputs/outputs but not all, the mapping is incomplete. It is kept, but the checks below wait until every step has both.

Inputs and outputs (a warning), for a mapped schema, walking the steps in order:

  • no two steps create the same output;

  • no step reads a variable that only a later step creates;

  • if the data's columns are known, every input is either a column or the output of an earlier step.

Usage

validate_schema(x)

Arguments

x

A schema object.

Value

x, invisibly.

See also

update_io() and update_data() to fix what it reports, and validate_script() to check the generated code by running it.

Examples

schema <- build_schema(data = data.frame(x = 1:3)) |>
  add_step(id = "a", decision = "d", inputs = "x", outputs = "y") |>
  add_step(id = "b", decision = "d", inputs = "y", outputs = "z")

# an edit made directly on the tibble skips the checks...
schema$inputs[[2]] <- "w"

# ...so run them yourself
validate_schema(schema)
#> Warning: The schema's inputs/outputs have 1 problem:
#> ! Step `b` reads `w`, which is neither a data column nor created by an earlier
#>   step.
